    40→### Site plan trigger and path

    46→### Subchapter E applicability and compliance tier (LDC Subchapter E, § 1.2)
    47→
    48→- Subchapter E applies if (a) project requires a site plan under Chapter 25-5, (b) site is **not** in a categorically exempt regulating plan area, and (c) the specific standard is triggered by the project's principal street type per Table A.

These plans *each impose their own* form standards — exemption from Subchapter E ≠ exemption from form rules.

   123→### Block circulation and large-site rules (Subchapter E § 2.2.5, § 2.3.1.B.2)

   125→- Sites ≥ 5 acres on CTC or Urban Roadway (any zoning), or ≥ 5 acres on Suburban/HCR (non-residential), must comply with internal block + ICR standards.

   127→- ≥15-acre sites may have one block up to 10 acres per 30 acres of site area (800-ft face still applies).
   128→- Suburban residential-only >5 acres: exempt from § 2.2.5.A–G but internal block perimeter capped at 2,700 ft.

   131→### Mechanical / refuse / screening (Subchapter E § 2.6)
   132→
   133→- Equipment, transformers, dumpsters must be screened from public streets, adjacent residential, and parkland.
   134→- Dumpster enclosures per City of Austin standard detail.
   135→- **AEC not available for § 2.6** — must comply or use Minor Modification.
   136→
   137→### Overlay-driven approval gates
   138→
   139→- **Waterfront Overlay** (any "-WO" suffix): PARD director sign-off (§ 25-2-721(A)(2)); Waterfront Planning Advisory Board recommendation; North Shore Central has 70° envelope and natural-materials rules; Rainey Street has 150-ft Lake / 50-ft Waller Creek setbacks (§ 25-2-739(B)); pedestrian-oriented use ≥ 50% of net usable ground floor adjacent to Town Lake in NSC, SSC, Auditorium Shores, Butler Shores, City Hall subdistricts (§ 25-2-692).    140→- **Waller Creek District** (geographic, no zoning suffix): exempt from Subchapter E, requires Urban Design Division coordination + Waller Creek Design Group review.
   141→- **UNO**: BCM 12.1 articulation point system; § 25-2-759 ≥42% occupant space; Urban Design Division design guidelines compliance determined by NPZD director.
   142→- **Downtown Creeks (DC)**: within 60 ft of downtown creek centerlines on CBD/DMU; max height 60 ft; first-floor glass VT ≥ 0.6 (§ 25-2-643(E)).
   143→- **DDBP** (Downtown Density Bonus Program, § 25-2-586): pre-approval *before* site plan submittal for any FAR/height above base. Rainey enters DDBP only above 8:1 FAR or 350 ft (§ 25-2-739(C)(5)). DDBP = Downtown Density Bonus Program — never "Design Build Plan."
   144→- **TOD / NBG / ERC regulating plans**: each has its own Active Edge map, building placement, building design, AEC, and compatibility rules — read the plan, not Subchapter E.
   145→
   146→### CBD/DMU specifics
   147→
   148→- Max front and street-side yard setback 10 ft for first four stories above grade (§ 25-2-594) — i.e., build-to at the property line.
   149→
   150→### Pre-application meeting
   151→
   152→- Strongly advisable for any project with overlays, AEC pursuit, or large-site block circulation. Lock in principal-street designation, Subchapter E applicability/tier, and AEC path.
   153→- Required for AEC: concept plan ≥ 10 days before pre-app conference.
   154→
   155→## Opportunities to evaluate
   156→
   157→- **Site Plan Lite** — confirm against current § 25-5 use list and size caps. If eligible, saves ~3–6 months.
   158→- **Categorical Subchapter E exemption** — sites in NBG/ERC/Plaza Saltillo/East MLK/Lamar-Justin/Waller Creek/Downtown/Airport Boulevard areas swap Subchapter E for the regulating plan; net effect often *more* design demand but a single coherent ruleset and clearer AEC pathways.
   159→- **Great Streets program participation** (downtown) — exempts site from CTC/Urban Roadway sidewalk + supplemental zone obligations under § 2.2.2.B and § 2.2.3.B; trade is the Great Streets streetscape build, often value-add for marketing.
   160→- **DDBP** — purchases FAR + height above base zoning entitlement in exchange for community benefits (affordability, open space). Plan early; gatekeeper requirements precede site plan.
   161→- **Minor Modification** (Subchapter E § 1.4) — up to 10% deviation from any numeric Subchapter E standard; up to 20% to protect a natural feature; unlimited to preserve a Heritage Tree. Director-approved in writing — much faster than AEC.
   162→- **AEC** (§ 1.5) — alternative equivalent compliance for §§ 2.2, 2.3, 2.5, 2.7, 2.8, Article 3. Not available for § 2.4 entrances or § 2.6 screening. Needs concept plan ≥10 days pre-app; expires 3 yr (one 1-yr ext).
   163→- **Industrial / warehouse off-CTC exemption** — confirm GFA breakdown and CTC status; full Subchapter E exemption available if criteria met.
   164→- **PUD** — if site is in a PUD, PUD standards govern *to the extent of conflict*; can selectively avoid specific Subchapter E provisions but doesn't categorically exempt.
   165→- **Mueller PUD** — categorically exempt from Subchapter E (§ 1.2.4.A.5) and Subchapter F (§ 1.3.2); governed by Mueller Design Book.
   166→- **ERC Hubs (Figure 1-6)** — exempt from ERC compatibility (§ 4.2.4) and eligible for ERC development bonus (Article 6).
   167→- **VMU / DB90 / DBETOD / Affordability Unlocked overlays** (cross-reference `zlu`) — affect setbacks/height that interact with build-to and parking placement. Pull from `programs.md`.

   172→- **programs.md** — Site Plan Lite eligibility check, DDBP eligibility, Great Streets boundary check, Mueller PUD check, ERC Hub check, density bonus stack (DB90, DBETOD, VMU, AU).
   173→- **phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md** — net site area; building GFA + per-use GFA breakdown (especially for industrial/warehouse exemption test); proposed building footprint and frontage occupation %; entrance location(s); curb cuts / drive aisles; parking count + structure type; rough massing (basewall height, total height, step-back assumptions); planned use mix (commercial vs. residential vs. industrial).
   174→- **adjacent_context** (surveyor) — abutting street classifications (ASMP level, named-corridor segment match), adjacent zoning (compatibility triggers), parkland adjacency, creek adjacency.
   175→- **property_profile** (surveyor COA GIS) — regulating plan layers, CTC layer, etod-subdistricts layer, parkland-deficient layer, watershed regulation areas, historic district intersect.

   177→## Output structure
   178→
   179→Standard discipline output shape. See `references/phase3-disciplines.md`.

   181→## Severity heuristics
   182→
   183→| Finding | Severity |
   184→|---|---|
   185→| Site falls within categorically exempt regulating plan (NBG/ERC/TOD/Waller Creek/Downtown/Airport Blvd) and applicant has not loaded the alternate ruleset | `significant` (re-plan required) |
   186→| Project triggers commission-level review or DDBP gatekeeper not yet engaged | `significant` (3–6 mo schedule + public-hearing risk) |
   187→| Principal street is a CTC segment that owner has misidentified or missed | `significant` (build-to, parking, entrance all change) |
   188→| Build-to % unmet on principal street | `significant` (form fix typically requires re-massing) |
   189→| Entrance placement violates § 2.4 — no AEC path available | `significant` |
   190→| WO subdistrict triggers PARD sign-off, WPAB review, or pedestrian-oriented-use 50% rule not factored | `significant` |
   191→| North Shore Central 70° envelope or Rainey 150/50 ft setbacks reduce buildable envelope | `significant` |
   192→| Mechanical / refuse screening missing from concept (cannot AEC § 2.6) | `moderate` |
   193→| Glazing %, VT, articulation, basewall step-back deviations within Minor Modification (≤10%) | `moderate` (path exists) |
   194→| Large site (≥ 5 ac) on CTC/Urban Roadway needs internal block + ICR + Table B layout | `moderate` |
   195→| Active Edge designation on a frontage drives 100% build-to and active-use mandate | `moderate` to `significant` |
   196→| Site Plan Lite eligibility (confirmed against use list + size caps) | `opportunity` |
   197→| Great Streets participation available for downtown sites | `opportunity` |
   198→| DDBP, ERC Bonus, Mueller PUD, off-CTC industrial exemption available | `opportunity` |
   199→| Project triggers permit-only path, no site plan required | `note` (favorable) |
   200→| Principal-street designation ambiguous on multi-frontage site | `data-gap` |
   201→| Subchapter E applicability tier (Full vs Partial) not determinable from facts | `data-gap` |
   202→| Active Edge designation cannot be confirmed without regulating plan map reference | `data-gap` |
   203→
   204→## Common pitfalls
   205→
   206→- **Treating "PUD" as a blanket Subchapter E exemption.** PUD supersedes only to the extent of conflict (§ 1.2.5.B.2.g). Provisions the PUD is silent on (often § 2.5 lighting, § 2.6 screening, Article 3 building design) still apply.
   207→- **Citing § 1.2.4.A.12 exemption while still loading Subchapter E notes on the cover sheet.** If the site is in NBG/ERC/TOD/Waller Creek/Downtown/Airport Blvd, all Subchapter E references must be removed and the regulating plan loaded instead.
   208→- **Claiming the industrial / warehouse exemption without verifying CTC status and GFA breakdown.** Both exemptions vanish on a CTC. Warehouse exemption needs <25% non-industrial GFA per building, documented.
   209→- **Asserting Chapter 245 vested rights without a Director-issued Vested Rights Determination letter** (§ 25-1-541). Even with a valid VRD, Subchapter E design standards still apply.
   210→- **Pursuing AEC for § 2.4 entrances or § 2.6 screening.** Categorically unavailable; must comply or use Minor Modification.
   211→- **Building to 50% on a CTC** because of an outdated 50% reference. CTC build-to is 75% in current Subchapter E and current regulating plans.
   212→- **Confusing principal street with frontages.** Principal street drives build-to, parking, entrance; *every* abutting frontage drives its own sidewalk + supplemental zone (§ 2.2.1.B).
   213→- **Missing the 75-ft entrance interval long-wall treatment.** Not a hard fail but adds substantial façade cost that should be budgeted at concept.
   214→- **Designating Active Edge from project narrative alone.** Confirm against the regulating plan figure (NBG Fig 1-2; ERC Fig 1-4; Plaza Saltillo / East MLK / Lamar-Justin Fig 2-1).
   215→- **Misidentifying admin-eligible projects as commission-required, or vice versa.** Build a defensible reading at concept; budget commission timeline if any waiver is contemplated.
   216→- **Missing WO subdistrict-specific rules** (Butler Shores 60% glazing facing Town Lake parkland; North Shore Central 70° envelope; Rainey 150/50 ft setbacks). All "-WO" sites get general WO; subdistrict overlays stack on top.
   217→- **Treating "pedestrian-scale" design as satisfying "pedestrian-oriented use."** The latter is a closed list in § 25-2-691(C).
   218→- **Skipping pre-application meeting on overlay-heavy sites.** Cheapest insurance against late-stage staff reinterpretation.
   219→- **Expanding DDBP as "Downtown Design Build Plan."** It is "Downtown Density Bonus Program" (§ 25-2-586(A)(1)).
   220→- **Confusing site plan with building permit.** Site plan establishes the envelope (build-to, entrance, sidewalk, screening); building permit follows and inherits.

    70→## 4. Legal Framework: Deed Restrictions vs. Zoning
    71→
    72→### Texas Law
    73→
    74→| Principle | Detail |
    75→|---|---|
    76→| Private enforcement | CC&Rs are private contracts enforceable by the HOA or individual lot owners through civil courts, not through city code enforcement |
    77→| City cannot override | The City of Austin cannot waive or override private deed restrictions through zoning changes, including HOME Initiative amendments |
    78→| Statute of limitations | Under Texas Property Code § 202.003, restrictive covenants in subdivisions with a property owners' association may be enforced indefinitely (no automatic expiration) |
    79→| Amendment process | CC&Rs can typically be amended by a vote of the membership (usually requiring a supermajority, e.g., 67% or 75% of lot owners), or by petition under Texas Property Code Chapter 209 |
    80→

    82→
    83→The HOME Initiative Phase 1 (Ord. 20231207-001) amended Austin's Land Development Code to permit duplexes by right on SF-2 lots. However:

    85→- **HOME does not preempt private deed restrictions.** If the Scofield Farms CC&Rs restrict lots to single-family use, a duplex remains prohibited as a matter of private covenant regardless of city zoning.
    86→- The city will issue a building permit for a duplex if the project meets zoning and code requirements — but the permit does not immunize the owner from HOA enforcement action.
    87→- The HOA or individual lot owners could seek injunctive relief (a court order to stop or reverse construction) if the project violates the CC&Rs.

# Site Plan & Form Findings — 12713 Cinchring Ln

**Property:** 12713 Cinchring Ln, Austin, TX 78727 — Lot 12, Block M, Scofield Subdivision
**Zoning:** SF-2 (Single-Family Residential — Standard Lot)
**Proposed use:** Demolish existing SFR (1993); build ground-up duplex (2 units)
**Lot area:** ~7,840 sq ft (0.18 acres)
**Date:** 2026-06-03

---

## Summary

- **The duplex is exempt from site plan under LDC Chapter 25-5.** Residential uses of four or fewer units do not trigger site plan review. The project proceeds via residential building permit only — no administrative site plan, no Site Plan Lite, no commission review.
- **No rezoning, conditional use permit, or Board of Adjustment action is required.** HOME Phase 1 permits a duplex by right on SF-2 lots. The procedural path is a straightforward residential building permit through Austin DSD.
- **Subchapter E (Design Standards and Mixed Use) does not apply.** Subchapter E is triggered only when a project requires a site plan under Chapter 25-5. Because the duplex is site-plan-exempt, no build-to, glazing, entrance orientation, articulation, or sidewalk-zone standards under Subchapter E attach.
- **McMansion / Subchapter F standards are superseded by HOME Phase 1 for two-unit development.** HOME Phase 1 incorporated the favorable Subchapter F setback reductions (15 ft front, 5 ft rear) and eliminated sidewall articulation and tent requirements for duplex/two-unit uses on SF lots.
- **Demolition of the 1993 house requires a separate demolition permit and an asbestos survey.** Pre-2000 construction triggers TCEQ Asbestos NESHAP survey requirements before any demolition work begins.

---

## Findings

### 1. Site Plan Exemption

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | opportunity |
| **Citation** | LDC Chapter 25-5 (site plan exemptions); LDC § 25-5-1 et seq. |
| **Finding** | A duplex (2 units) on an existing platted lot is exempt from site plan requirements under Austin LDC. The Chapter 25-5 exemption applies to residential uses of four or fewer units. No administrative site plan, Site Plan Lite, or commission site plan is required. |
| **Implication** | This eliminates 6-9 months of site plan review timeline and associated engineering costs. The project proceeds directly to residential building permit, with an expected review timeline of 4-8 weeks. No Subchapter E compliance is triggered. No pre-application conference is needed. |
| **Recommended next step** | Confirm exemption at DSD intake. File residential building permit application directly. |

### 2. Procedural Path — Residential Building Permit Only

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | note |
| **Citation** | HOME Phase 1 (Ord. 20231207-001, effective Feb 5, 2024); LDC § 25-2-492 |
| **Finding** | HOME Phase 1 permits a duplex by right on SF-2 lots with no rezoning, no conditional use permit, and no Board of Adjustment variance. The lot at ~7,840 sq ft exceeds the 5,750 sq ft minimum lot area. The project requires only a residential building permit reviewed by DSD for compliance with LDC dimensional standards and IRC/IBC building codes. |
| **Implication** | The entitlement path is the simplest available under Austin's LDC. No public hearing, no discretionary approval, no neighborhood notification under zoning review. The only discretionary review risk is the HOA Architectural Control Committee (private covenant, outside city jurisdiction). |
| **Recommended next step** | Prepare building plans per HOME Phase 1 dimensional standards (40% building coverage, 0.40:1 FAR, 35 ft height, 45% IC) and submit to DSD residential plan review. |

### 3. Subchapter E Does Not Apply

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | note |
| **Citation** | LDC Subchapter E, § 1.2 (Applicability); LDC Chapter 25-5 |
| **Finding** | Subchapter E applies only when a project requires a site plan under Chapter 25-5 (§ 1.2.1). Because this duplex is site-plan-exempt, Subchapter E design standards — including build-to percentages, ground-floor glazing minimums, entrance orientation requirements, sidewalk zone dimensions, parking placement rules, and articulation standards — do not apply to this project. |
| **Implication** | The developer has full design flexibility on facade treatment, entrance placement, glazing, and building orientation. No build-to percentage, no principal-street glazing minimum, no supplemental zone requirement. This substantially simplifies design and reduces facade cost. |
| **Recommended next step** | No action required. Do not load Subchapter E standards onto permit drawings. |

### 4. McMansion / Subchapter F — Superseded by HOME Phase 1

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | note |
| **Citation** | HOME Phase 1 (Ord. 20231207-001); LDC Subchapter F (Residential Design and Compatibility Standards) |
| **Finding** | HOME Phase 1 incorporated Subchapter F's favorable setback reductions for two-unit and three-unit uses on SF lots (front setback reduced from 25 ft to 15 ft; rear from 10 ft to 5 ft). HOME also eliminated the McMansion sidewall articulation requirement and the tent/envelope requirement for duplex projects. The simplified design standards under HOME govern instead of the full Subchapter F framework. |
| **Implication** | The designer does not need to comply with the McMansion tent envelope, sidewall articulation, or street-facing garage limitations that apply to single-family construction in SF-2. However, FAR (0.40:1) and building coverage (40%) still apply and are the primary massing constraints on this lot. |
| **Recommended next step** | Design to HOME Phase 1 dimensional standards. Note the 25 ft platted building line (see Finding 6) may override the 15 ft HOME front setback. |

### 5. Cinchring Lane — Level 1 Local Street, No Frontage Requirements

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | note |
| **Citation** | Austin Strategic Mobility Plan (ASMP) Street Network Table; LDC Subchapter E § 2.1 (principal street hierarchy) |
| **Finding** | Cinchring Lane is a Level 1 local residential street under the ASMP (50 ft ROW, 2 lanes, ~500 vpd, 25 mph). It is not a Core Transit Corridor (CTC), Urban Roadway, or Suburban Roadway under Subchapter E's principal street hierarchy. Even if Subchapter E applied (which it does not), a Level 1 local street would impose no build-to percentage, no glazing minimum, no entrance orientation mandate, and no parking placement restriction. |
| **Implication** | No frontage-driven form requirements from any source. No ROW dedication is anticipated (existing ROW meets Level 1 standard). No scenic roadway overlay applies. |
| **Recommended next step** | None required. |

### 6. Platted 25-Foot Building Line — May Override HOME Front Setback

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | moderate |
| **Citation** | Plat, Vol. 11863, Pg. 1147, Travis County; HOME Phase 1 (15 ft front setback for duplex) |
| **Finding** | The recorded plat shows a 25-foot building line on the front of Lot 12. HOME Phase 1 reduces the zoning front setback to 15 ft for duplex uses. However, the platted building line is a recorded encumbrance. Under Austin practice, the more restrictive requirement controls — meaning the 25 ft platted building line likely governs over the 15 ft zoning setback at the permitting counter. |
| **Implication** | If the 25 ft building line is enforced through DSD plan review, the buildable depth is reduced by 10 ft compared to the HOME setback. On a lot of this size, that is a meaningful reduction in buildable area. To use the 15 ft setback, the owner would need to replat or amend the plat — which triggers subdivision review and adds timeline and cost. |
| **Recommended next step** | Confirm with DSD whether the platted building line is enforced at building permit review or treated as a private covenant only. If enforced, design to the 25 ft front setback. If a replat is desired, budget 3-6 months and engage a surveyor. |

### 7. Demolition Permit and Asbestos Survey

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | moderate |
| **Citation** | TCEQ 30 TAC Chapter 113, Subchapter B (Asbestos NESHAP); Austin DSD demolition permit process |
| **Finding** | The existing house was built in 1993 — pre-2000 construction that may contain asbestos-containing materials (ACM) in roofing, siding, joint compound, floor tile, pipe insulation, or vermiculite attic insulation. TCEQ Asbestos NESHAP regulations require a thorough asbestos inspection by a licensed Texas asbestos inspector before any demolition. If ACM is found, abatement must be performed by a licensed contractor with proper notification to TCEQ before demolition proceeds. A separate demolition permit from Austin DSD is required; typical turnaround is 2-4 weeks. |
| **Implication** | The asbestos survey must be completed before demolition permit issuance. If ACM is found, abatement adds cost ($3,000-$15,000 depending on extent) and 2-4 weeks to the pre-construction timeline. Failure to survey before demolition is a TCEQ violation with significant penalties. Lead-based paint (LBP) is also a concern for pre-1978 construction but is less likely in a 1993 house (post-ban). |
| **Recommended next step** | Engage a licensed Texas asbestos inspector to perform a pre-demolition survey. Budget for potential ACM abatement. File demolition permit with DSD after survey is complete. |

### 8. Building Separation — IRC Fire Separation, No Zoning Minimum

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | note |
| **Citation** | HOME Phase 1 dimensional standards; IRC R302.1 (exterior walls — fire separation distance) |
| **Finding** | HOME Phase 1 eliminated any zoning-based minimum building separation requirement for duplex units. The only separation requirement is the IRC fire-separation-distance standard: if the exterior wall is less than 3 feet from the lot line or from another building on the same lot, fire-resistance-rated construction is required per IRC R302.1 (1-hour fire-resistive construction, no openings). For a duplex with attached units sharing a common wall, the shared wall must be a 1-hour fire-rated assembly per IRC R302. For detached duplex units, fire separation distance governs openings and fire-resistance rating of exterior walls. |
| **Implication** | The developer has flexibility to build attached (side-by-side or stacked) or detached units. Attached construction with a 1-hour rated party wall is the most space-efficient configuration on a 7,840 sq ft lot. If detached, wall openings and projections near the property line or the other unit are restricted by IRC fire separation distance requirements. |
| **Recommended next step** | Coordinate with the architect and building code consultant on the fire separation assembly for the chosen configuration (attached vs. detached). |

### 9. Drainage Review Exemption

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | opportunity |
| **Citation** | Site Plan Lite Phase 2 drainage reforms (adopted Mar 6, 2025); LDC residential infill provisions |
| **Finding** | Under the Site Plan Lite Phase 2 drainage reforms, lots of 11,500 sq ft or less do not require drainage review. This lot at ~7,840 sq ft qualifies for the exemption. No engineered drainage study, no on-site detention pond, and no formal drainage plan submission is required, provided the site drains to the street or existing drainage infrastructure. |
| **Implication** | This eliminates the cost of an engineered drainage study (typically $5,000-$15,000) and the space burden of an on-site detention facility. The lot drains to the existing Scofield subdivision storm drainage system. |
| **Recommended next step** | Confirm drainage exemption eligibility at DSD intake. Ensure site grading directs runoff to the street or existing drainage system. |

### 10. No Overlay-Driven Design Review

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | note |
| **Citation** | LDC Chapter 25-2 (overlay districts); Austin GIS |
| **Finding** | The property is not within any overlay or combining district that would impose additional design review: no NCCD, no NP combining district, no Waterfront Overlay, no UNO, no Downtown Creeks, no Waller Creek District, no Historic District, no scenic roadway overlay, no ETOD overlay. No DDBP, VMU, or DB90 combining district applies. The property is not within any adopted regulating plan area (NBG, ERC, Plaza Saltillo, East MLK, Lamar/Justin Lane, Airport Boulevard, Downtown Austin Plan). |
| **Implication** | No additional design review gates, no advisory board reviews, no design commission hearings. The project is subject only to base SF-2 zoning standards as modified by HOME Phase 1 and applicable building codes. |
| **Recommended next step** | None required. |

### 11. HOA Architectural Control Committee — Private Covenant Risk

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | significant |
| **Citation** | Scofield Farms Declaration of CC&Rs, Vol. 11863, Pg. 1147, Travis County; Texas Property Code Chapter 202 |
| **Finding** | The Scofield Farms ROA maintains an Architectural Control Committee (ACC) that reviews and must approve all exterior construction. The CC&Rs almost certainly restrict lots to single-family residential use — standard for 1980s-90s Texas subdivision declarations. HOME Phase 1 does not override private deed restrictions. If the CC&Rs prohibit duplex use, the HOA or individual lot owners could seek injunctive relief to block construction, even after a city building permit is issued. The full CC&R text has not been obtained — this remains a critical data gap. |
| **Implication** | This is outside the city's site-plan and building-permit framework, but it is the single largest feasibility risk for the project. A building permit does not immunize the owner from HOA enforcement. If the CC&Rs restrict to single-family use, the developer faces litigation risk or must obtain a CC&R amendment (requiring supermajority vote of ~574 homeowners) or HOA waiver. |
| **Recommended next step** | Obtain and review the full Declaration of CC&Rs and all 8 amendments from the Travis County Clerk or Inframark. Engage a Texas real estate attorney to evaluate the specific use-restriction language and enforcement risk before committing to design. |

### 12. No Concept Plan Provided

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | data-gap |
| **Citation** | N/A |
| **Finding** | No concept plan, site plan, or preliminary building design was provided for review. Specific building footprint, unit configuration (attached vs. detached, side-by-side vs. stacked), entrance placement, driveway location, and massing cannot be evaluated against the dimensional envelope. |
| **Implication** | The findings above address regulatory applicability and procedural path but cannot assess whether the proposed building fits within the 40% building coverage / 0.40:1 FAR / 45% IC envelope, or whether the 25 ft platted building line creates a design constraint for the intended program. |
| **Recommended next step** | Prepare a preliminary site plan showing building footprint, setbacks (using 25 ft front until platted building line is resolved), driveway, and impervious cover calculation. Verify that the duplex program fits within the FAR and coverage limits. |

---

## Open Questions for the Engineer

1. **Platted building line enforcement:** Does Austin DSD enforce the 25 ft platted building line at residential building permit review, or is it treated as a private covenant enforceable only by neighbors/HOA? This determines whether the effective front setback is 15 ft (HOME) or 25 ft (plat).

2. **Lot width:** Does the lot meet the 50 ft minimum lot width required for duplex use under HOME Phase 1? The plat (Cabinet 91, Slides 264-265) should be reviewed to confirm lot dimensions.

3. **Asbestos survey results:** Has an asbestos inspection been performed on the 1993 house? If ACM is identified, what is the estimated abatement scope and cost?

4. **Unit configuration:** Are the two duplex units planned as attached (common party wall) or detached? This drives the IRC fire separation assembly requirements and affects building coverage efficiency.

5. **FAR feasibility:** At 0.40:1 FAR on ~7,840 sq ft, the maximum gross floor area is ~3,136 sq ft for both units combined. Does the intended unit program (number of bedrooms, unit sizes) fit within this limit? If a two-story design is contemplated, the 40% building coverage still caps the footprint at ~3,136 sq ft, but FAR governs total floor area across both stories.

6. **5-ft PUE location:** Where does the 5-foot public utility easement run on this lot (front, side, or both)? Structures and permanent improvements are prohibited within the PUE, which further constrains the buildable area.

7. **Existing sanitary sewer vault:** What is the disposition plan for the concrete sanitary sewer vault identified on site? Will it be removed, capped, or re-used? Coordinate with Austin Water.

8. **Tree survey:** Are there any protected trees (8 in. diameter or greater) or heritage trees (19 in. or greater) on the lot that would require preservation or mitigation?
